approach: The problem still exists: `critic_brief` (`crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs:185-210`) prints only the plan under review, and `critic_round` builds `CriticInputs` with only the current plan and Athena's findings (`crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:353-359`). From round 2 on, code adds a section "Earlier rounds on this plan" before "Plan under review". For each earlier critic round it prints the findings the planner was shown (the stored critique's findings, Athena's and the critic's; the critic's `Fix:` text is already inside the evidence, `run/mod.rs:355`). For a round before the last, the planner's answer is the approach and decisions of the plan that followed it. For the last earlier round the answer is the plan under review itself, which is not repeated; the brief says so and gives a code-computed list of what changed since the last reviewed plan, compared item by item on exact text. The history comes from `closing.plans` and `closing.critiques`, which `end_round` fills in step (`planning.rs:483-484`), through a new pure builder `earlier_rounds` in `planning.rs` and a new in-memory `EarlierRound { plan, findings }` brief input. Nothing is stored and no record type is added. `critic.md` gets two bullets (about 439 bytes; the frame bound allows 461, `lib.rs:570`). Bullet A: from round 2 check that each earlier blocker and major was resolved, and raise any that was not again at its earlier severity, so an ignored major still forces a round through `plan_verdict` (`run/mod.rs:364`). Bullet B limits only new majors: a new major only on a part the brief lists as changed or new, or on a defect earlier rounds missed that stops the plan working or leaves a criterion unshown, with file:line evidence; any other new finding is minor, even where a rule above says major. The brief's intro says a changed Approach alone does not make any other item changed. Round 1's brief, the planner brief, the 5-round cap and the any-major-forces-a-round rule are not touched. No refusal or matching rule is added (`plan_changes` only describes differences), so the refusal corpus does not apply.

decisions.choice: Code supplies what changed. A private `plan_changes(previous, current)` in planner.rs (`pub(super)` so the briefs.rs tests call it) compares the last reviewed plan with the plan under review one item at a time with a small `Item` enum deriving PartialEq over the record structs (approach, steps and open questions compared trimmed). The brief prints 'Changed or new: ...', 'Removed: ...' (only when non-empty) and 'Every other part is unchanged since round M.', or 'Nothing changed: the plan under review is identical to the round M plan.' Labels are short (Approach; Decision i: first 60 chars; File path; Step i: first 60 chars; Risk: ...; Dependent name; Demonstration for criterion c; Open question: ...). Order is ignored. The brief's intro paragraph also says: 'A changed Approach alone does not make any other item changed: a decision, file, step, risk, dependent, demonstration or open question is listed only when its own text changed.'
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3 (the approach is one free-text item that nearly every revision rewrites, so 'Approach' will almost always be listed; `plan_body` prints it as one item, briefs/plan.rs:52). The intro sentence stops a changed approach from widening the 'changed parts' limit to the whole plan, because each other item is compared on its own text. D189's Tradeoff also states the remaining limit: a major tied to the approach text is still allowed every round. The critic cannot infer what changed from findings alone, so code computes it (the mechanism default). Only the last reviewed plan is compared, because that is the plan the critic last judged in full. Labels, not plan text, keep the section small. An item reworded without a real change is listed as changed, which only lets the critic look again and never hides a change.

rejected.option: Show every earlier plan in full
rejected.why: Each round adds a whole plan of several KB; the brief grows without bound and the critic still has to diff by eye.

rejected.option: Ask the critic in prose to compare with what it remembers
rejected.why: The critic is a fresh invocation each round and remembers nothing; this is the failure the request describes, and the mechanism default forbids relying on prose.
One inserted step would mark every later step as changed. Matching on exact item text ignores position.

rejected.option: Show a line diff of the rendered plan bodies
rejected.why: A line diff needs long context to read and breaks on harmless re-wrapping; labelled items match how the critic's findings cite locations.

rejected.option: Treat the approach as unchanged-by-default or drop it from the list
rejected.why: A revision that changes the approach has changed something the critic should judge; hiding it would hide a change.

decisions.choice: The critic.md rule keeps an unresolved earlier finding at its earlier severity and limits only NEW majors. Two list items are appended after the 'In round one' line (line 16), each on its own line, verbatim: (A) '- From round 2, check that each earlier blocker and major finding was resolved in the plan under review; raise any that was not again at its earlier severity.' (B) '- From round 2, raise a new major only on a part the brief lists as changed or new, or on a defect earlier rounds missed that stops the plan working or leaves a criterion unshown, with file:line evidence; report any other new finding as minor, even where a rule above says major.' The two lines are about 439 bytes (A 159, B 280, counted by hand); the producer keeps the sum at or under 461 and the frame test checks it.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The previous bullet B said 'otherwise minor' about any major on an unchanged part, which also downgraded an earlier major the planner ignored: that finding was raised before, so it is not 'missed', and A set no severity. Now A says an unresolved earlier finding is raised again at its earlier severity, and `plan_verdict` (`run/mod.rs:364-374`, called at `planning.rs:426`; tests at `run/tests.rs:31-64`) still turns any accept with a blocker or major into revise, so ignoring a major keeps forcing a round. B says 'a new major only', so it limits new findings only. B still gives way to a real missed defect: it needs to stop the plan working or leave a criterion unshown, and needs file:line evidence, which answers the request's 'a real defect it can show was missed before'. Changed or new parts keep every existing rule. The frame is 2236+439=2675 bytes, 892 estimated tokens, under the 900 bound (`estimate_tokens(frame.text) < 900`, `lib.rs:570`); ceil(2697/3) is 899, so 22 bytes of slack remain. Line 16 ('In round one') already scopes an earlier rule by round, so the pattern exists. D189 marks the critic's rating as prose-only (model judgment); the history itself is supplied by code.

rejected.why: It downgrades an ignored earlier major, so a plan that ignored a finding could be accepted (finding 2).

decisions.choice: Answer shape. For each earlier round before the last, print "Planner's answer (the round k+1 plan):" with its approach and each decision as 'n. choice Reason: reason' (no rejected options). For the last earlier round, print "Planner's answer: the plan under review below (round N)." and then the changed list, with no repeat of the plan's approach or decisions.
decisions.reason: The latest answer is the plan under review, so repeating it prints the same text twice and blurs which copy is under review. Older answers appear nowhere else in the brief, so they are printed. At the 5-round cap there are at most 3 older answers.

rejected.option: Print approach and decisions for the latest round as well
rejected.why: Duplicates the plan body and confuses which copy to review.

rejected.option: Print no older answers, only findings and the changed list

decisions.choice: History data model: `EarlierRound { plan: JobPlan, findings: Vec<Finding> }` in the context crate, one per earlier round, oldest first. `earlier_rounds(plans, critiques, before_round)` in planning.rs pairs each critique with the plan of the same round in `closing.plans` and skips a critique with no plan. The brief derives each round's answer from the next entry's plan, or from `inputs.plan` for the last. No field is added to JobPlan, Critique or PlanOutput.
decisions.reason: `end_round` pushes the reviewed plan and its critique together (planning.rs:483-484); `stop_on_mechanical_limit` pushes both (312-313) and the preflight stop pushes the plan alone (350), then planning ends, so inside the loop the two lists line up by round. `Closing::new()` is built fresh per run (mod.rs:1362) and `plan_round` is called once (mod.rs:1372), so the lists hold only this job's rounds (a resumed job's seed comes from an earlier job, mod.rs:1366-1370, and gives its first critic round no history). A mechanical pass returns `RoundEnd::Mechanical` without pushing (planning.rs:251-269), so a plan sent back by Athena's own checks is never a round. Criterion 4 forbids a new record type.

rejected.why: Changes the planner's output schema and prompt (out of scope), every plan fixture and a `deny_unknown_fields` record (records/plan.rs:95-97); the plan text already holds the answer.

decisions.choice:
Prove 'identical to today's output' with a recorded digest plus exact structure checks that do not depend on step order. Before editing `critic_brief`, add `critic_brief_without_earlier_rounds_is_todays_brief`: it takes `critic_brief(&critic_inputs())`, cuts it from '## History file' to the end (the tail), hashes the tail with `athena_data::sha256_hex` and asserts the digest equals a literal recorded from the unmodified code. In the same test, without the digest: (a) the tail's lines that start '## ' equal exactly ["## History file", "## Plan under review (round 1)", "## Athena's own findings on this plan", "## Soundness", "## Critique"]; (b) the tail contains `format!("## Plan under review (round 1)

{body}
## Athena's own findings on this plan

")` where `body` is `super::plan::plan_body` of `plan(1)`; (c) the brief ends with 'End with the critique as your structured output.
'; (d) no '## Earlier rounds'; (e) the brief equals the with-history brief after the text from '## Earlier rounds' up to '## Plan under review' is removed. D189's Provenance bullet records the digest literal and the pre-edit run (command and result), so the verifier can match the test's literal against a stated pre-edit run.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. A digest alone is an oracle only if it was recorded before the edit, and the verifier sees only the final tree. Checks (a) to (c) pin the tail's exact shape by hand-written text and the shared `plan_body` renderer (unchanged), so they hold or fail regardless of when the digest was taken, and the Provenance record lets the verifier match the digest to a stated pre-edit run. The old critic tests check substrings only (briefs.rs:2859-2961), so without this a stray change outside the section would pass. The tail holds everything the change can touch (the insertion point, plan body, Athena's findings, soundness, critique). The head (title, request, reading, system facts) is left out of the digest on purpose: it embeds the live `defaults.toml` through `AcceptedReading::new(&reading(), &defaults(), ..)` (briefs.rs:2952, 1604-1606) and `SYSTEM_FACTS` (briefs.rs:1500), which this change itself edits; check (e) covers the head.

risks.risk: A critic told to treat unchanged parts leniently may miss a real defect in them, and a critic may not follow the two bullets at all.
risks.mitigation: Bullet B limits only NEW majors on unchanged parts to a defect that stops the plan working or leaves a criterion unshown, with file:line evidence, and says that rule wins over the always-major lines. Bullet A keeps an unresolved earlier finding at its earlier severity, and `plan_verdict` (run/mod.rs:364) still turns any major into a revise. Changed and new parts keep every rule. D189 and the changelog state that the critic's rating is prose-only and that whether a model critic follows the bullets, and how many 5-round stops this prevents, is not measured.

risks.risk: The approach is one free-text item that nearly every revision rewrites, so 'Approach' will almost always be listed as changed and a major tied to the approach text is always allowed.
risks.mitigation: The brief's intro says a changed Approach alone does not make any other item changed, each other item is compared on its own text, and test (3) shows an approach-only change lists only 'Approach'. D189's Tradeoff states the remaining limit.

risks.risk: A planner that rewords an untouched item without changing it makes that item look changed, so the critic may raise a major on it.
risks.mitigation: The comparison is by exact text, trimmed, and ignores order, so it errs toward listing a reworded item as changed, which lets the critic look again and never hides a change. Covered by `critic_brief_plan_changes_compare_items_by_exact_text`.

risks.risk: critic.md has only about 22 bytes of slack under the 900-token frame bound, and the facts line could be forgotten.
risks.mitigation: The two bullets are given verbatim (about 439 bytes against a limit of 461). The frame-size test and the budgets test fail loudly if the producer lengthens them, and the producer sets the facts line from the budgets test's failure message.

risks.risk: The critic brief grows each round, which adds cost to later critic calls.
risks.mitigation: At the 5-round cap the brief holds at most 4 rounds of findings, 3 older answers (approach and decision text, no rejected options) and one label list. This is an estimate of a few KB, not measured. The caps are per invocation and do not read brief size (planning.rs:347).

risks.risk: The recorded digest in `critic_brief_without_earlier_rounds_is_todays_brief` breaks when another job edits the critic brief's fixed text, and the verifier cannot prove from the final tree that it was recorded before the edit.
risks.mitigation: The digest covers fixed text and the `plan(1)` fixture only. The test also asserts the tail's exact heading order, the exact plan block and the exact last line by hand-written text, which do not depend on when the digest was taken. D189's Provenance bullet records the digest and the pre-edit command run. The failure message prints the new digest; a legitimate edit of the brief's fixed text updates the literal in the same change.

risks.risk: The first critic round of a resumed job has no history (its seed comes from an earlier job, mod.rs:1366-1370).
risks.mitigation: The limit is stated in the changelog and D189. The seed's findings still reach the planner as before; round 1's brief stays unchanged, as the accepted reading says. The existing `a_retry_of_a_job_stopped_in_planning_carries_the_last_critiques_findings` (job_plan.rs:1042) covers the resumed path for the reader brief.

risks.risk: docs/system-facts.md is not in the reading's deliverable list, so a scope check could flag it.
risks.mitigation: The edit is one number, forced by budgets.rs:124-129 once critic.md grows; the file is not governance (admission.rs:36-41, 63-68) and is a planned file in this plan, so the verifier does not count it as unplanned (plan.rs:177-180).

demonstrations.method: Add `the_second_critic_brief_carries_round_ones_findings_and_the_planners_answer` to crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs. It builds `Fixture::with_config(&planned_config())` and a `Scenario` with two plans and two critiques. Plan 1 is `good_plan()`. Plan 2 is `good_plan()` with `approach` set to 'ANSWER-MARK add the greeting line and its test.' and `steps` set to ['Edit README.md.', 'STEP-MARK add the greeting test.']. Critique 1 is `critique_of("revise", &[("major", FINDING)], None)` (job_plan.rs:462-476, which sets the finding's summary to FINDING and its location to 'demonstrations'); critique 2 is `critique_of("accept", &[], None)`. The script is `scenario.script()` wrapped in a closure that pushes each `Role::Critic` `user_prompt` into a shared Vec (the wrapper pattern at job_plan.rs:1054-1061). The test calls `athena.ask` and `athena.go` and asserts the job lands. Critic brief 0 holds neither FINDING nor 'Earlier rounds on this plan'. Critic brief 1 holds '## Earlier rounds on this plan', '### Round 1: findings', FINDING with its '[major] (critic) at demonstrations' prefix, "Planner's answer: the plan under review below (round 2).", the exact line 'Changed or new: Approach; Step 2: STEP-MARK add the greeting test.' and 'Every other part is unchanged since round 1.'. It holds 'ANSWER-MARK' exactly once (the plan body, not the history) and does not hold the round-1 approach text 'Add a greeting line to README.md.' anywhere before '## Plan under review'.
demonstrations.observes: Two critic prompts are captured through the real planning path (`Athena::go` -> `plan_round` -> `critic_round`). The first has no history. The second has round 1's finding, the planner's answer (the plan under review plus the code-computed change list) and no duplicate of the answer text.
demonstrations.fails_without: Before the change the round-2 critic brief has no 'Earlier rounds on this plan' section, no round-1 finding text, no 'Planner's answer' line and no changed-items line, so the first assertion on critic brief 1 fails. The test compiles on the old code (it uses only public API).
